## onchain-billing-reconcile — stuck `reserved` row reconciliation (task 015-18, deployment.md §10.8, data-model.md §4.6.5, R-14)

**Every 15 minutes**, applied, not measured. A `client_usage` row a process died between reserving
and completing stays `'reserved'` forever unless this closes it. A row can be visibly stuck for at
most ThresholdMs + cadence = 120 000 + 900 000 = 1 020 000 ms before this job closes it — the bound
`deployment.md` §10.8 states.

**One SQL operator does the transition AND the refund.** n8n gives no transaction between two
nodes, so a "close, then credit" pair would leave a window where a row is closed but not yet
credited (task 015-10, MAJOR-A round 2 of the architecture review). `Refund expired` is that one
operator: it also skips the credit when `access_profile_id IS NULL` (the local principal) or when
`credits_balance_raw IS NULL` (`credits_mode = 'unlimited'`).

**Drain, don't take one batch and stop.** `More to close?` loops back to `Refund expired` while a
batch comes back FULL (`BatchSize = 500`) and the cap (`MaxBatches = 20`) is not yet reached. Hitting
the cap while still full means real backlog remains — `detail_json.batchExhausted = true` and
`Check backlog` throws so the alert reaches Telegram through `onchain-error-alert`. The run still
writes `outcome = 'ok'`: it closed everything it found, and `outcome`'s dictionary is closed to two
values (data-model.md §4.5.9) — `batchExhausted` is the separate, named observable.

**`ThresholdMs` below 120 000 ms is refused, not honoured.** A lower value would refund the reserve
of a request that is still executing — money for work not yet done. A refused run still writes its
row, with `outcome = 'failed'` and the rejected setting named in `detail_json`; `Check backlog`
throws for this case too.

**Period in the `retention_runs` row is derived, never typed in.** `period_from = 0`,
`period_to = startedAt − ThresholdMs` — the SAME horizon the operator's own `WHERE` clause reads, so
the row can never name a period the run did not actually cover (MINOR-8 round 1).

**Credential: `Onchain engine state`, NOT `Supabase DB`** — the same state-role credential
`onchain-retention` uses (`deployment.md` §10.5). The snapshotter's role holds no grant on
`client_usage`; a Postgres refusal to read it with this credential is a check, not a convention.
After the WI-62 container move (task 015-21/015-23), this credential is retargeted to the new
container — task 015-22's job, not this one's.

**Why a SEPARATE workflow from `onchain-retention`, not a fourth job in it.** One Schedule trigger
carries one cadence; `onchain-retention` runs once a day, and a job needing a materially tighter
cadence needs its own trigger.

**Installation requires the owner's explicit approval, exactly as `onchain-retention` does**
(`deployment.md` §10.6.1, §10.8). This task describes and exports the workflow; it does not create
or activate it on the shared instance — the billing ledger this job reconciles lives only on the
WI-62 container, which does not exist until tasks 015-21/015-23 land.

parameters.query:
WITH p AS (SELECT convert_from(decode($1,'base64'),'utf8')::jsonb AS j),
     pick AS (
       SELECT id FROM onchain.client_usage
        WHERE state = 'reserved'
          AND reserved_at < (SELECT (j->>'horizon')::bigint FROM p)
        ORDER BY reserved_at
        LIMIT (SELECT (j->>'batchSize')::int FROM p)
        FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
     ),
     closed AS (
       UPDATE onchain.client_usage c
          SET state = 'refunded', refund_reason = 'expired',
              terminal_at = (SELECT (j->>'nowMs')::bigint FROM p),
              updated_at  = (SELECT (j->>'nowMs')::bigint FROM p)
         FROM pick
        WHERE c.id = pick.id AND c.state = 'reserved'
       RETURNING c.access_profile_id, c.price_raw
     ),
     credited AS (
       UPDATE onchain.access_profiles pr
          SET credits_balance_raw = (pr.credits_balance_raw::numeric + s.sum_raw)::text
         FROM (SELECT access_profile_id, SUM(price_raw::numeric) AS sum_raw
                 FROM closed WHERE access_profile_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1) s
        WHERE pr.id = s.access_profile_id
          AND pr.credits_balance_raw IS NOT NULL
       RETURNING 1
     )
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM closed)::bigint    AS rows_affected,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM credited)::bigint  AS profiles_credited;

nodes.name: More to close?
nodes.notes: Bare `$json` here is DELIBERATE, against CLAUDE.n8n.md's own "never bare $json.field" rule. That rule exists so an inserted upstream node cannot silently repoint a reference — but the insert-safe form it prescribes, `$('Tally').item.json.continueLoop`, is the one form that breaks INSIDE this back-edge loop: a referenced node inside a loop resolves to its LAST run, not to the run that produced the item now being evaluated (the same cross-iteration gotcha `Plan run`'s own comment cites for `$('Tally').all()`). `$json` is the current item, which is exactly what this condition must test. A node inserted between `Tally` and here must therefore carry `continueLoop` through, or move this condition with it.

INSERT INTO onchain.retention_runs
  (id, job, target_table, period_from, period_to, rows_affected, started_at, finished_at, outcome, detail_json)
SELECT id, job, target_table, period_from, period_to, rows_affected, started_at, finished_at, outcome, detail_json
FROM jsonb_to_recordset(convert_from(decode($1,'base64'),'utf8')::jsonb)
  AS x(id text, job text, target_table text, period_from bigint, period_to bigint,
       rows_affected bigint, started_at bigint, finished_at bigint, outcome text, detail_json text)
ON CONFLICT (job, period_from, period_to, started_at) DO NOTHING;
